text:
sarah: Quick heads-up: scheduling planned maintenance to roll firmware on the VPC egress router that services Dedicated/private workloads in us-west2. Aiming for a short window tomorrow 2025-11-07 02:00–02:30 UTC. Expect possible 30–120s transient request failures during each router failover. No DB/data migration.

mike: tagging infra-ops + oncall. Are we able to tighten to 02:05–02:20 to reduce customer impact?

maria: oncall has capacity then. Two-minute staggered draining between routers — so max single-client impact should be small but some requests may get 502s. We'll circuit-break and retry clients downstream.

linda: please confirm whether this affects Hosted API customers (public hosted) vs Dedicated/private. I assume only Dedicated/private in that region?

sarah: correct — only Dedicated/private VPC peered routers in us-west2. Hosted API unaffected.

incident-bot: @channel Reminder scheduled event: "VPC Router Firmware Roll" at 2025-11-07 02:00 UTC. Assigned: sarah, mike. Expected impact: brief request failures for Dedicated/private us-west2.

cs-lead: Can we get a customer-facing blurb + statuspage text? We should notify customers on Dedicated plans and Solutions contacts.

mike: Draft status page entry below — please edit:```Scheduled Maintenance — VPC router firmware update
Start: 2025-11-07 02:00 UTC
End: 2025-11-07 02:30 UTC (expected)
Impact: Customers using Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments in us-west2 may experience brief request errors (HTTP 502/503) and elevated latency for up to 2 minutes per failover. No data loss expected.
What we are doing: Applying vendor-recommended firmware to improve stability and security.
Workaround: Clients should implement standard retry/backoff. We will post updates here and via email to affected accounts.```

maria: statuspage-bot, can you stage that as a scheduled maintenance entry (private customers only) and set reminder 1h before?

statuspage-bot: Scheduled maintenance created (ID: maint-20251107-01). Reminder set 1 hour prior. Visibility: Customers with Dedicated/Private subscriptions in us-west2.

sarah: Customer email / portal note draft for cs-team:```Subject: Planned maintenance: short interruption for Dedicated/private us-west2
Hi —
We will perform a firmware update on the VPC egress router serving Dedicated and Private deployments in the us-west2 region on 2025-11-07 02:00–02:30 UTC. During the work we may see brief request errors (502/503) and transient latency spikes for a few seconds to up to ~2 minutes per router failover. No data loss expected. If you have critical traffic during that window and cannot tolerate retries, please reply and we'll coordinate an alternative window.
Thanks,
Redwood Inference Operations
```

cs-lead: Looks good. Add a line about support contact and post-mortem if customers request more details.

mike: Added. Also attaching the internal rollback/runbook snippet for oncall:```- Pre-checks: verify health of both routers and BGP sessions
- Step 1: cordon router-A, drain flows (script: ./drain-router.sh router-A)
- Step 2: apply firmware (vendor image v1.2.3)
- Step 3: monitor traffic and metrics for 5m; if errors > 1% rollback
- Rollback: restore previous image and re-enable router; open incident if rollback occurs
- Post: post update to statuspage + close maintenance```

linda: I'm going to send the customer email to the affected list now and copy cs-lead. I'll wait until statuspage is in draft.

statuspage-bot: Maintenance entry moved to 'scheduled' and queued for 1 hour prior reminder.

sarah: small change — window shortened to 02:05–02:20 UTC (reduced by stagger). Update statuspage & email accordingly.

mike: acknowledged. Updating drafts. New statuspage text pushed. statuspage-bot, update start/end times.

statuspage-bot: Maintenance maint-20251107-01 updated: Start 2025-11-07 02:05 UTC; End 2025-11-07 02:20 UTC. Reminder updated.

maria: oncall note: I'll be beside the runbook during the window. Mike will be stand-by network. Sarah, you'll coordinate post-notify?

sarah: yes — I'll post completion notice and send follow-up to customers with brief summary and telemetry (error rate during window).

incident-bot: @here Maintenance started: VPC Router Firmware Roll (maint-20251107-01) — 2025-11-07 02:05 UTC. Assigned: sarah, maria, mike.

maria: Starting drain of router-A now. Running: ./drain-router.sh router-A — ETA ~90s.

mike: Applying firmware to router-A. Watching metrics.

maria: router-A back up, traffic restored. Observed <0.6% 502 spike for ~40s. Proceeding to router-B.

mike: router-B firmware apply in progress.

maria: router-B back up. Observed ~1.1% 502 spike for ~70s during roll, fell back to baseline after retries. No rollbacks.

sarah: All done. No rollback required. Moving maintenance to completed and posting final update.

statuspage-bot: Maintenance maint-20251107-01 completed at 2025-11-07 02:18 UTC.

sarah: Final customer-facing completion blurb:```Maintenance completed (2025-11-07 02:18 UTC): Firmware upgrades applied to VPC routers in us-west2. During the window some Dedicated/private requests experienced brief errors (peak ~1.1% 502s, lasted <90s). No data loss. If you saw persistent errors after 02:20 UTC please open a support case and include request IDs.```

cs-lead: Thanks — I'll send the post-notify to affected accounts and follow up for any requested post-mortem.

linda: Closing the loop with solutions engineering to confirm customer-specific mitigations were OK.

sarah: Closing thread. If anyone needs logs/metrics I posted them to the incident runbook page (link in #eng-sre). :white_check_mark:"
